subject: [PATCH RFC v4 05/12] mm/gup: add get_user_page_vma() to fault in a page under a held lock

2026-07-24.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function, get_user_page_vma(), which allows faulting in a single page under a held lock. The function is designed to be used by __access_remote_vm() when it needs to access a page that is not already present in the page tables. It takes advantage of the existing VMA locking mechanism and simplifies the process of accessing remote memory. If the fault cannot complete under the per-VMA lock, the function releases the lock and returns -EAGAIN for both the mmap lock and the per-VMA lock. The patch also updates the handling of VM_FAULT_ERROR to return -EFAULT instead of BUG().

reviews.author: Suren Baghdasaryan
reviews.summary:
The reviewer pointed out a mistake in the patch description, specifically that there is no lock to drop under the per-VMA lock, and suggested renaming the @locked parameter to @mmap_locked for clarity.

Reviewer Suren Baghdasaryan expressed concern that the patch removes a comment explaining why -EAGAIN is returned after fault handling, and requested its reinstatement for clarity when using mmap_lock.

Reviewer Suren Baghdasaryan questioned the logic of returning -EAGAIN when handle_mm_fault() under per-VMA locks returns an unexpected value, suggesting that instead, -EAGAIN should be returned to retry under mmap_lock for a definitive result.

Reviewer Suren Baghdasaryan questioned why the patch changes the return value of -EAGAIN to -EFAULT even when operating under mmap_lock, requesting clarification on the reason behind this change.

Reviewer Suren Baghdasaryan questioned whether get_user_page_vma() should validate the VMA only once at the caller level, rather than for each page, and asked if relying on the caller to do this is acceptable.
reviews.raw_body:
"There is no such lock to drop under the per-VMA lock" is a bit
confusing. Maybe change it to "Under per-VMA lock we are not holding
mmap_lock, therefore @locked is not modified."
To avoid more confusion I would rename @locked parameter in this
function to @mmap_locked. I think that would make things more clear.

---

This comment explains why after completing the fault handling we still
return -EAGAIN. I think it's still relevant for when we use mmap_lock.
Why are you removing it?

---

I don't follow this logic. If handle_mm_fault() under per-VMA locks
returns something unexpected, shouldn't we return -EAGAIN to retry
under mmap_lock and get the definitive result?

---

This changes the returned error code even when we operate under
mmpa_lock. What's the reason for it?

---

I assume get_user_page_vma() will be called multiple times for the
same VMA. Would it make sense to validate the VMA only once (at the
level of the caller) instead of doing that for each page? Of you don't
want to rely on the caller to do that?

reviews.author: John Hubbard
reviews.summary:
Reviewer John Hubbard noted that the get_user_page_vma() function does not handle the case where a page is already mapped in the VMA's page tables, and requested that the function check for this condition before attempting to fault in the page.

The reviewer pointed out a difference in behavior between VM_IO and VM_PFNMAP VMA types, noting that VM_IO only indicates that MM callers should not inspect the mapped pages due to side effects, whereas VM_PFNMAP identifies mappings whose COWed pages should be returned. The reviewer suggested testing for VM_PFNMAP specifically instead of treating both as exceptions.
reviews.raw_body:
On 7/24/26 3:29 PM, Rik van Riel wrote:
...

---

This treats VM_IO and VM_PFNMAP as the same exception, but they have
different meanings. VM_IO tells MM callers not to inspect the mapped
pages because accesses can have side effects. It does not imply that
the VMA contains raw PFNs!

For example, sg_mmap() creates a VM_IO-only VMA whose fault handler
installs ordinary pages from the SCSI reserve buffer. If such a page is
already present, follow_page_mask() returns it before the pfnmap test
below is reached. Patch 6 then lets /proc/PID/mem and ptrace copy that
page directly, even though sg provides no ->access callback and the
operation fails today. Writes can also modify the buffer when the
mapping is writable. Existing ptrace authorization still applies, so
this is not a privilege bypass, but it removes the VM_IO exclusion for
a driver that did not opt in through ->access.

An untouched page in the same VMA still fails because pfnmap is also
true for VM_IO and this function refuses to fault it. The result
therefore depends on whether the target previously touched the page.
The required exception is narrower. A remap_pfn_range() VMA has both
VM_IO and VM_PFNMAP, but VM_PFNMAP is what identifies the mapping whose
COWed page should be returned. 

So if you use the FOLL_PFNMAP_COW flag suggested on patch 4, and test
only VM_PFNMAP here:

	ret = check_vma_flags(vma, gup_flags);
	if (ret)
		goto fail;
	pfnmap = vma->vm_flags & VM_PFNMAP;

Patch 6 can set FOLL_PFNMAP_COW for __access_remote_vm().
check_vma_flags() then permits VM_IO | VM_PFNMAP for that caller while
continuing to reject VM_IO-only mappings. vm_normal_page() supplies the
remaining distinction: it returns the COWed normal page and rejects the
raw PFN.

Something like that.

thanks,
-- 
John Hubbard

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function called get_user_page_vma() to the Linux kernel's mm/gup.c file. It is designed to fault in a single page under a held lock, either the mmap lock or the per-VMA lock. The function simplifies __get_user_pages() by walking the page tables with follow_page_mask(), faults in missing pages with faultin_page(), and returns the page with a reference still held by the caller. It also includes checks for VM_IO/VM_PFNMAP VMA exceptions, userfaultfd VMA handling, and error cases where the lock is released and -EAGAIN is returned.
